title: Blind Signatures for Untraceable Payments
bookTitle: Advances in Cryptology: Proceedings of Crypto 82
abstractNote: Summary (paraphrase, not the original abstract): introduces blind signatures, which let a bank sign a message without seeing it, as the basis for untraceable electronic payments.

title: A Digital Currency Architecture for Privacy and Owner-Custodianship
abstractNote: Summary (paraphrase, not the original abstract): proposes a privately operated, government-backed digital currency in which users hold funds in wallets that hide their payment counterparties, aiming for cash-like privacy and personal control while keeping a regulatory role for banks.

title: Can Cryptocurrencies Preserve Privacy and Comply with Regulations?
abstractNote: Summary (paraphrase, not the original abstract): argues that cryptocurrencies fall short of cash-like anonymity, rejects a choice between total surveillance and unregulated secrecy, and proposes two compromise approaches that give regulators auditability while protecting users.

title: A Decentralised Digital Identity Architecture
abstractNote: Summary (paraphrase, not the original abstract): argues that digital identity systems should protect human rights by letting people keep several unlinked identities, and proposes a decentralised, standards-based design built on distributed ledger technology.

title: Privacy by Design in Value-Exchange Systems
abstractNote: Summary (paraphrase, not the original abstract): examines the most disputed privacy issues in electronic payment systems, especially proposals for central bank digital currency.

title: Decentralised Trust for the Digital Economy
abstractNote: Summary (paraphrase, not the original abstract): a research proposal arguing that activity records on platforms enable surveillance and discrimination, and calling for systems that let individuals build trust and communicate on their own terms.

title: The Development of Central Bank Digital Currency in China: An Analysis
abstractNote: Summary (paraphrase, not the original abstract): finds the People's Bank of China digital currency plan broadly sound and the most advanced globally, but argues it overlooks issues such as treating wallets as accounts, and recommends privacy-preserving, non-custodial wallets.

title: The Right Place at the Right Time
abstractNote: Summary (paraphrase, not the original abstract): examines the use of network location in authentication and abuse prevention.

title: Response to "The digital pound: a new form of money for households and businesses?"
abstractNote: Summary (paraphrase, not the original abstract): a consultation response arguing the proposed digital pound lacks a clear motivation and falls short on privacy, custody, identity and ledger design, and calling for a privacy-by-design, decentralised alternative.

title: Private Electronic Payments with Self-Custody and Zero-Knowledge Verified Reissuance
abstractNote: Summary (paraphrase, not the original abstract): extends a privacy-focused digital payment protocol so reissued money can be verified as created only by the original issuer, using an audit log and zero-knowledge proofs that protect payer anonymity.

title: Protocol-Embedded Compliance for Privacy-Preserving, Non-Custodial Digital Payments
abstractNote: Summary (paraphrase, not the original abstract): argues digital cash-like assets can meet compliance and audit needs without custodial intermediaries, by having independent entities sign compliance attestations that become part of each asset's own state.

title: Designing Partitioned Digital Asset Infrastructure
abstractNote: Summary (paraphrase, not the original abstract): argues digital payments need not rely on third-party custodians, and that privacy-preserving e-cash tokens held outside accounts could separate payment services from banking.
